According to the Article 317 clause (3), another way of removal is prescribed on some other grounds as, the President may by orders remove the chairman or any other member of a public service commission, if the chairman or member is adjudged an insolventi; or engages during his term of office in any outside, paid employment; or is unfit to continue in office due to infirmity of mind or body, in the opinion of the President.

s: A joint state public service commission may be established for two or more states.
o: A prospective States agree in this regard
Parliament appoints joint state public service com-
x: According to Article 315(2) of Indian Constitution, two or more states may agree that there shall be one public service commission for that group of states and if a resolution to that effect is passed by houses or where there are two houses, by each house of the legislature of those states, parliament may be law provide for appointment of a joint state public service commission.

s: Choose the correct alternative: The Chairman of a Joint Public Service Commission for two or more States is appointed by –
o: The President of India on the recommendation of the
The Governor of the largest State
A Committee of Governors of all the States concerned
x: According to Article 316(1), the Chairman and other members of the Public Service Commission shall be appointed in case of Union Commission or Joint Commission by the President of India and in case of State Commission by the Governor of the State.

s: The Chairman of a Joint Public Service Commission for two or more states is appointed by
o: the President of India on the recommendation of the Governors concerned.
a committee of Governors of all the states concerned.
x: A Joint SPSC's chairman and members are appointed by the President, not by Governors or a committee of them. Only the State PSC is appointed by the Governor.

s: A Joint Public Service Commission for two or more States can be established by
o: Parliament, if requested by concerned States
x: A JSPSC is created by an Act of Parliament when the Legislatures of two or more States pass resolutions requesting it (Art. 315(2)). Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha or UPSC alone cannot create it.
